title: Wavelet Convolutions for Large Receptive Fields
mechanism: Convolution applied to wavelet subbands, giving very large receptive fields with log-growing parameters, more shape bias and more robustness to corruption.
adaptation: WTConvNeXt-T (timm) encoder in U-Net++, or WTConv2d replacing the 3x3 convs in ResNet-34 layer3/4. A whole-cell receptive field should help the half-cut layout and long scuff streaks on E1.
min_experiment: Arm: WTConvNeXt-T U-Net++ under PF, 5 seeds. Baseline: ImageNet ConvNeXt-T U-Net++ under PF and the house model. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2, test crack IoU. Kill: E1 relF1@2 < +0.03.
evidence: R: ImageNet-1K top-1 82.5 / 83.6 / 84.1 (T/S/B, README); better corruption robustness and shape bias.
prior_overlap: Only the DINOv3 vs ImageNet ConvNeXt-T 2-seed F51 screen was run; WTConv was never tested.

alt_notes.adaptation: WTConvNeXt-T as U-Net++ encoder or WTConv2d in ResNet-34 layer3/4; whole-cell context for half-cut layout and long scuffs on E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: WTConvNeXt-T U-Net++ under PF vs ImageNet ConvNeXt-T under PF, 5 seeds, test + E1; kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.03.
